tagline.text: A community-run eco-town in western Cebu, known for its mangrove river cruise

location.label: Location
location.text: Western coast of Cebu Province, about 60–90 km southwest of Cebu City (varies by route)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: One day or 2 days and 1 night

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–2,500 (per person, a day trip from Cebu City)

children.text: Aloguinsan is a small town on the Tañon Strait coast of western Cebu, famous for a mangrove river cruise and for eco-cultural tours run directly by villagers. It suits travelers who want a quiet day on a river, at sea and among local people rather than at a beach resort.

Aloguinsan is a small municipality of about 35,000 people on the west coast of mainland Cebu, facing the Tañon Strait. It borders Pinamungajan to the north, Carcar to the east and Barili to the south, and covers roughly 62 km². It began as a settlement under Pinamungajan and became its own town in 1886 by a Spanish-era decree; the story goes that the town's history started with a watchtower built on a hill at the river mouth to watch for Moro raiders.

The villagers are what turned this town into a destination. The Bojo Aloguinsan Ecotourism Association (BAETAS) was founded in 2009 and runs the Bojo River cruise, protecting the mangroves at the river mouth and the coral along the coast while channeling the fees into village incomes. Accounts often mention that this work won an ASEAN tourism award in the community category. There are almost no large hotels or resorts, so most people visit as a day trip from Cebu City, but that also means the place lacks the usual hustle of a tourist spot.

The signature activity is the Bojo River cruise. In a paddled bangka you drift about 1.4 km down between mangroves and nipa palm walls to the river mouth, where the river water meets the blue sea, then come back, with a swim stop along the way. Most visitors combine it with lunch at the village farm restaurant The Farmhouse, a mat-weaving demonstration and snorkeling at Hermit's Cove on the coast, making a half-day to full-day outing.

It is close to the city yet quiet, so it works well as a day away from Mactan or Cebu City. Combine it with Mantayupan Falls in neighboring Barili to the south and the old town of Carcar to the east, and you have a full western Cebu day. Price lists are widely shared online but no official rate card is published, so check current prices and the tide with the tourism office before you go.
Village fishermen paddle a bangka for about
1.4km

down the river between mangroves and back. Birds and crabs can be seen along the shallow edges, and the meeting of blue sea and green river water at the mouth is striking. There is a swim stop, so bring swimwear and a change of clothes.
A bamboo boardwalk of about

runs through the mangroves by the river, and climbing roughly 150 steps brings you to a viewing gazebo. Before or after the cruise you can walk it and hear a short explanation of the mangroves and the wildlife.

This is a farm restaurant run by the community group CHAT. A typical visit walks through the vegetable garden, chicken coop, worm compost area and tilapia pond, includes a demonstration of making puso (rice cooked in a woven palm-leaf pouch), and ends with a buffet lunch. Pick-and-pay harvesting is also said to be possible.
This cove on the Kantabogon coast is about
5 minutes

by bangka from the town center. Inside an 18-hectare marine protected area you can see coral, tropical fish and sea turtles with a local guide, according to accounts. It is a rocky shore rather than a sand beach and the water gets deep quickly, so think of it as a snorkeling spot.

Before the cruise there may be a send-off ritual by a village medicine man and a mat-weaving demonstration, and a cultural performance or bird-watching tour can be added on request. It is closer to showing what villagers actually do than to a staged tourist show, which makes it a good fit for families with children.

The student-group package includes the town's fort site (the Baluarte Heritage Park), the old stone church and the lighthouse (parola). Individual travelers can also take a short walk there around lunch since it is close to the town center. Aloguinsan is said to be the only parish in the Archdiocese of Cebu dedicated to the Archangel Raphael.

The patron saint's feast falls on the second Sunday of June, and the Kinsan Festival runs for about a month around then. Kinsan is a dotted grouper caught in large numbers from May to July, and fish dishes and street events are timed to that season. Dates change every year, so check the latest announcements.

The coast also has a secluded beach, true to its name, and small resorts. Entrance was listed at about ₱15 per person in a 2021 guide (it depends on where you enter) and ₱50 for adults in a 2023 guide, which also noted the resort was temporarily closed. Prices and operations may have changed, so confirm the current fee and whether it is open before you go.

items.title: Day trip
items.subtitle: A full day on the Bojo River from Cebu City

children.text: Board a bus to Aloguinsan (or Pinamungajan) at the Cebu South Bus Terminal. This timing lets you make a morning cruise.
Get off at the Aloguinsan public market or in front of The Farmhouse and register. From the market to the Bojo River jump-off by motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) takes about
10 minutes
Hear the welcome briefing and take the Bojo River cruise. Because the boats are paddled, it takes about
1 hour
, and there is a swim stop.
Have lunch at a village restaurant while watching the mat-weaving demonstration.
Move to Hermit's Cove for snorkeling, or look around the old church and the Baluarte in town.
Head back to Cebu City by bus or van. Allow for rush-hour traffic and leave by 4 PM at the latest.
The paddled boats reportedly cannot run at full low tide. Check the tide before you leave and book a time close to high tide.

items.title: 2 days and 1 night in western Cebu
items.subtitle: Linking Aloguinsan with the falls in Barili

children.text: Leave the Cebu South Bus Terminal for Aloguinsan.
Spend the first morning on the Bojo River cruise and lunch at The Farmhouse.
Snorkel at Hermit's Cove and check in at a village stay (a homestay or a small guesthouse).
Have grilled fish and puso for dinner at a restaurant near the town market and turn in early.
On the second morning, take a bus south to the center of Barili.
See Mantayupan Falls, and stop at the Barili milk station on the way back.
Travel times and connecting buses on day two vary with local conditions. See the Barili entry as well for the falls route.
A direct flight from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Mactan-Cebu Airport (CEB) takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Several airlines, including Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific, fly daily.
From Mactan Airport through Cebu City to the South Bus Terminal takes about
40 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes
by taxi or Grab, depending heavily on traffic.
From the Cebu South Bus Terminal, yellow buses and minibuses run to Aloguinsan or Pinamungajan. The trip takes about
2–3 hours
, and two guides list a one-way fare of about
Get off at the Aloguinsan public market, or ask to be dropped "in front of The Farmhouse" if you are heading to the river. Guides disagree on where to get off, so confirm with the conductor.
From Cebu City, drive the national road via Toledo or via Carcar, which takes about
2 hours
. Depending on the guide, the distance is about
58km
(via Carcar) to
72km
(via Toledo).
Enter "Bojo River Aloguinsan" in your navigation app. Park in the open lot near the jump-off.
From the public market to the Bojo River takes about
10 minutes
by motorcycle taxi. The local government and tourism groups are said to have set a fare table, so check before you ride.
Hermit's Cove is about
5 minutes
by bangka from town, or you can go by motorcycle.
Local fares change often. Ask the tourism office or your lodging staff for current prices before you ride.
The best season for Aloguinsan is the dry season,
December–May
. Clear skies sharpen the contrast between the green river and the blue sea at the mouth, and swimming is pleasant. The midday sun is strong, so a hat and sunscreen are essential.
During the rainy season,
June–November

, afternoon showers are frequent and a swollen river can sometimes block the boat route. On the other hand the vegetation is green and there are fewer visitors. Paddled bangkas have trouble running at low tide, so checking the tide is important all year. Around the second Sunday of June, during the Kinsan Festival, the town is busy and lodging and transport fill up quickly.

Aloguinsan has almost no hotels or large resorts. Most visitors come on a day trip from Cebu City, but if you want to stay, there are small apartelles and homestays in town and small resorts along the coast. Rooms are few, so book ahead on holidays, and assume that convenience stores and ATMs exist only in the town center.

The food centers on seafood and farm produce. The buffet at The Farmhouse serves home-grown vegetables, tilapia and puso, and restaurants around the market sell grilled fish and soups cheaply. During the Kinsan Festival in June, dotted grouper (kinsan) dishes are popular. Because the community group provides lunch, a package that includes meals is better than eating at a walk-in restaurant.

Many guides advise booking the full package (lunch, snack and craft demo included) at least two days ahead through the Aloguinsan tourism office. The walk-in-only rate (about ₱400) does not include meals.
The paddled boats cannot run at full low tide. Check the tide table the day before and choose a time around high tide.
Since there is a swim stop, bring swimwear, a towel, a change of clothes and a waterproof bag. Life vests are provided.
A sign at the Bojo River entrance says it is fine to leave but not to leave your trash. Take your trash with you.
Prices differ by guide (₱650–850). When you register, first ask about group size and what is included.
Combining the trip with Mantayupan Falls in neighboring Barili to the south makes for a rewarding day. Allow for the travel time, and it is better to see one side in depth.
Bring plenty of cash. There are almost no ATMs in the village and few places take cards.

After the September 30, 2025 northern Cebu earthquake, repair work continues at facilities around Cebu. Check with the municipality and your lodging before you go to see whether facilities are operating.
There is no official published rate card or schedule, and blogs disagree. Prices in this guide are approximate.
Hermit's Cove is a rocky shore where the water gets deep quickly. Beginners should wear a life vest and swim close to the guide.
During rainy weather or typhoons the river may rise and boats may not run. Leave some slack in your schedule.
Do not touch or step on sea turtles or coral. Because it is a marine protected area, reef-friendly sunscreen is recommended.
Little is known about the last bus times. Return to the market area by 4 PM and confirm your ride back.
This is the tallest waterfall in Cebu, in neighboring Barili to the south, about
40 minutes to 1 hour
from Aloguinsan by car. See the
Mantayupan Falls
entry.
To the east is Carcar, with old Spanish-style buildings, street sights and mouth-watering market food. A common plan is to have lunch in
Carcar
on the way back.
This is a small lake toward Toledo City to the north. Accounts say some visitors stop here on the way back from the Bojo River. Check on site whether it is open.
Neighboring Barili to the south has a milk station and an old church besides the falls, which can extend into a full-day route.
